judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, absolute prohibition on commingling; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside 1.4 (nominee registration, use of a custodian) and 4.6 (bank deposits) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Flat prohibition on any action resulting in Investment Company Act registration; the term 'investment company' is a statutory one and is not left vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.1 expressly contemplates that the Trust may be 'required to comply with' the Investment Company Act and directs the Trustee to comply or qualify for exemption, which is difficult to reconcile with an absolute bar here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'limited to the extent, and in the manner provided in, the Plan' is clear in direction but supplies no content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It subordinates compensation to the Plan while 4.7(a) fixes hourly rates and lets the Trustee raise them annually without court approval, and 3.2 grants powers 'except as set forth in ... the Plan' — the priority ordering is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence is self-undercutting: approval is required to dispose of an asset worth $5,000 or more, then 'notwithstanding the foregoing' the Trustee may take 'any other action with respect to such assets' without approval — the boundary between disposal and 'any other action' is genuinely uncertain, as is whether $5,000 is per asset or per transaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Supervised by and shall report to the Committee' cannot easily coexist with 2.3's grant of 'exclusive authority over administration' to the Trustee, 3.5's 'without prior or further authorization', or 3.2(x)/(y)'s unqualified sale and abandonment powers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quorum definition overlaps at exactly three members (both limbs apply), and 'reasonable notice', 'means reasonable under the circumstances' and 'a period of time reasonable under the circumstances' for deemed email approval are vague where certainty matters.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 'any bylaws or other agreements to the contrary' and feeds the approval mechanism in 3.3(e) and the amendment power in 8.1; no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear referral of Trustee/Committee disputes to the Bankruptcy Court on five days' notice; 'for cause' shortening is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.4 makes the Bankruptcy Court's exclusive jurisdiction conditional on the Chapter 11 Case remaining pending, while this clause assumes that forum unconditionally — a gap that would matter after case closure (see 3.2(z)).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Holder access is conditioned on 'purposes reasonably related to such holder's interests', not being 'an undue burden', and not being 'detrimental to the Liquidating Trust' — three open-ended qualifiers that a Trustee and a holder could apply very differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.3 (holders have no administration rights) and 9.2 (privilege), and the last sentence expressly preserves privilege; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as otherwise set forth in this Trust Agreement or in the Plan ... but without prior or further authorization' is a self-cancelling formulation: the exception swallows the freedom it grants.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'without prior or further authorization' language is in direct tension with 3.3(e)'s requirement of Committee approval for dispositions of $5,000 or more and with the Committee's supervisory role.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'within a reasonable time after liquidation of all assets' is an open standard, and the section introduces distributions to Class 1 claim holders in a trust the rest of the document describes as existing solely for Class 2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Class 1 distribution sentence cannot be squared with the recitals' 'sole purpose ... for the benefit of the holders of allowed Class 2 claims', 1.1(a), 2.1 and 1.1(a)'s 'free and clear of any lien' transfer of the securing assets.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parentheses are unbalanced — '(including the receipt ... Internal Revenue Service) upon audit if not contested by the Trustee)' — so it is not clear what the 'upon audit' qualifier attaches to, and the section is misnumbered 3.8 (there is no 3.7).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A second, different section is also numbered 3.8 (Compliance with Laws), and grantor-trust filing must be read with 6.2's allocation mechanics and 9.1's tax-driven construction rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short catch-all filing obligation; 'any other statements, returns or disclosures ... required by any governmental authority' is broad but its content is set by law, not by the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 3.2(g), 6.1 and 6.2; the duplicate 3.8 numbering is the only oddity and does not affect this subsection's meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carries the same section number (3.8) as the preceding reporting section, and it presupposes 'proceeds of borrowings' — a category of transaction the section itself does not authorise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision of Article 3 grants a borrowing power, yet both this section and 4.7(b) ('unable to borrow funds ... in accordance with the terms of this Trust Agreement') assume one exists — an unresolved whole-instrument gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as permitted by herein' is ungrammatical, and the sentence structure ('solely in a fiduciary capacity ... and not otherwise, except that the Trustee may deal with the Trust Assets as permitted') creates an exception whose scope is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fiduciary-capacity-only rule must be read with 4.3(a)'s exculpation for all but gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud and with 4.2's 'reasonable business judgment' standard, which pull in different directions on the applicable duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'expeditious but orderly', 'timely' and 'not unduly prolong' are soft, and the power in (a) to sue 'whether or not such suits are brought in the name of the Liquidating Trust, the Trustee, the Debtor, the estate or otherwise' raises a real question about whose claims may be prosecuted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 3.1 and overlaps 3.2(d)/(v), while imposing a 'reasonable business judgment' duty that sits awkwardly with the 4.3(a) exculpation limited to gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out trio 'willful misconduct, gross negligence or fraud' is conventional and reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relaxes the 'reasonable business judgment' duty stated in 4.2 and the fiduciary-capacity rule in 4.1, and the same trio recurs in 4.3(c), 4.3(d), 4.7(a) and 5.2 — consistent usage but the duty/exculpation mismatch remains.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — 'their determinations shall not result in the imposition of liability upon the Trustee' — is awkward and arguably says something different from the reliance protection in the first sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 4.4's counsel-reliance protection but has to coexist with 4.3(a)'s gross negligence carve-out, since blind reliance could itself be grossly negligent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Indemnity for liabilities 'arising out of or due to their actions or omissions, or consequences of their actions or omissions' is very broad, but the proviso is a clear exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.3(f) makes the Trustee's indemnity secondary to insurance while this grant is unconditional, and 4.3(f) says nothing about the Committee — an asymmetry that would need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Advancement runs to 'the Trustee's or the Committee's' expenses, but the clawback obligation is imposed only on the Trustee, so nothing requires repayment by Committee members; that asymmetry is visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 4.3(c) (which indemnifies Committee members) and 4.3(f) (insurance priority for the Trustee only), the treatment of the Committee is inconsistent across the section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short survival clause; 'remain available to and be binding on' is slightly loose but not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 5's successor-trustee machinery, particularly 5.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the extent that it is not covered by insurance, if any' is clear in principle, though 'it' has no clean antecedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back the unconditional indemnity in 4.3(c) and depends on insurance the Trustee is only permitted, not required, to obtain under 3.2(m) — a real interaction a court could be asked to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard reliance clause; 'no reason to believe to be other than genuine' is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates part of 4.3(b) on counsel reliance without conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear third-party protection keyed to absence of actual knowledge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably insulates transactions the Trustee entered without the Committee approval required by 3.3(e), but that is the clause's evident purpose rather than an incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence ('shall be limited to include only those investments, or shall be expanded to include any additional investments, as the case may be') is clumsy but its effect — track what a liquidating trust may hold — is intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-referenced correctly from 3.2(s) and consistent with 3.3(a) and 3.3(c); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Trustee, and the Trustee and shall be entitled to reimbursement' is a plain mechanical error, and the rate table plus the unilateral annual increase power leaves unclear whether the increase is capped or reviewable at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Allowing the Trustee to raise her own compensation on ten days' notice 'without approval of the Bankruptcy Court' is hard to square with 3.3(d) (compensation limited as provided in the Plan) and with 3.3(e)'s Committee supervision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a long conditional but each condition is stated; 'reduce to cash that portion of the Trust Assets necessary' is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes a power to 'borrow funds ... in accordance with the terms of this Trust Agreement' that no provision of Article 3 confers, and any such reduction to cash above $5,000 would trigger 3.3(e)'s Committee approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Five words, entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere requires a bond; consistent with 3.3 and Article 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The temporal clause is garbled — 'while serving as Trustee under this Trust Agreement following the termination of this Trust Agreement or following the earlier of his or her removal or resignation' — with an omitted conjunction, so the duration of the confidentiality duty cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against 4.3(e) (provisions binding on former Trustees) and 5.4, which contemplate obligations surviving removal or resignation, but nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final clause is circular: service continues until 'the proposed effective date' unless the Court consents to an earlier effective date 'which shall be the date that appointment of a successor Trustee becomes effective' — the referent of 'which' and the operative date are both uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2 gives the Committee power to remove and replace the Trustee while this section vests successor appointment in the Bankruptcy Court, so the appointment mechanism is not uniform across Article 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term 'Cause' is carefully drawn but is then rendered largely pointless by the next sentence allowing Committee removal without cause, and 'unresolved material conflict of interest' and 'reasonable time' are open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Removal without cause by the Committee is difficult to reconcile with 2.3's exclusive-authority framing, with 5.1/5.3's Bankruptcy Court-centred appointment machinery, and with 3.3(g)'s referral of Trustee/Committee disputes to the court.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acceptance instrument 'in form satisfactory to the successor Trustee' makes the incoming trustee the sole judge of its own acceptance, which reads like a drafting slip (one would expect the Committee or the Court).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 procedurally, though it does not say who approves the appointment where the Committee rather than the Court makes it under 5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but orderly; the irrevocable power of attorney and its survival of incapacity are stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.1-5.3 and 4.3(e); no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The dangling 'if applicable' at the end of the first sentence leaves unclear whether it qualifies the state and local law exemption or the whole exemption, and 'as necessary' governs the SEC filing duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its instruction to comply with the Investment Company Act if required conflicts with 3.3(c), which forbids any action resulting in registration as an investment company, and its securities framing sits against 2.2's transfer restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Technical but internally complete tax-allocation mechanics; 'promptly following the end of each calendar year' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.8(a)'s grantor-trust filing position, 1.2's deemed transfer and 9.1; the reference to the Disclosure Statement is unincorporated but harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The regulation citation is garbled ('Section § 301.7701-A(d)'), and 'if any Trust Assets are not duly claimed' introduces an undefined concept for a trust whose interests are registered and uncertificated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing sentence letting the Trustee terminate 'without further order of the Bankruptcy Court' sits against the same section's requirement of court-approved extensions and against 3.2(z)'s closing reports; 'Reserved Claims' is again defined only in the Plan.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any substantive provision' implies a class of non-substantive provisions that may be amended without Committee approval, but the line is nowhere drawn — an expressio unius problem on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment by Trustee and Committee alone, without holder consent, must be read with 2.3 (holders have no rights), 9.1 (retroactive tax amendments) and 9.8 (Plan controls), which supply different amendment constraints.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It contains its own interpretive canon — 'any ambiguity herein shall be construed consistent herewith' — and authorises amendments that 'may apply retroactively', a phrase whose limits are unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unilateral-sounding amendment permission has to be reconciled with 8.1, which requires Committee approval for amendments, and with 9.8's rule that the Plan controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reasonably clear vesting of estate privileges with an unqualified waiver discretion; 'to the extent that the Debtor or the estate would be entitled' is a workable measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2(j) and with 3.4's final sentence protecting privileged material from holder access; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the powers, instructions, or funds in trust hereunder' is a slightly odd list, but the covenant itself is straightforward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports 1.1(a) and 1.1(c) and the disclaimer of reversionary interests matches 1.1(a)'s statement that the Debtor retains no interest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: California law is chosen alongside 'federal bankruptcy law to the extent applicable', and exclusive Bankruptcy Court jurisdiction is limited to 'so long as the Chapter 11 Case may be pending' — both qualifiers are the kind courts are regularly asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.3(g) sends Trustee/Committee disputes to the Bankruptcy Court without that pendency limit, and 9.8 subordinates this Agreement to the Plan's own retained-jurisdiction provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability, clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause specifies only deposit in the mail as sufficient giving and never states when notice is deemed received, and the sentence is broken by page artefacts; 'if no proof of claim has filed' is also ungrammatical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Other provisions contemplate email notice and approval (3.3(f)) and mailed notice of fee increases (4.7(a)), so whether this exclusive-sounding mail formula governs those is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It would blunt any argument built on the 3.3 heading ('Limitation of Trustee's Authority; Committee Approval') but does not conflict with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'incorporates the provisions of the Plan' is a very broad incorporation whose extent (all of the Plan, or only provisions relevant to the Trust) is not delimited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the instrument's own conflict rule and would be the pivot for every Plan-versus-Agreement question raised by 1.1(a), 1.2's Class 3 slip, 3.3(d) and 3.6's Class 1 distributions, so its operation is inherently relational.
